education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

METHODS  OF  SAMPLING  AND  PHYSICAL 
TESTS  FOR  REFRACTORY  MATERIALS 

PART  11     DETERMINATION  OF  WARPAGE

FOREWORD 

Methods  of  sampling  and  physical  tests  for  refractory  materials  were  originally  covered  in  IS  485  :  1953 
'Methods  of  sampling  and  testing  of  refractory  materials  (  tentative  )'.  This  Indian  Standard  was  first 
published  in  1962  on  methods  of  sampling  and.physical  testing  of  refractory  materials  and  subsequently 
revised  in  1974. 

Other  parts  of  this  standard  published  so  far,  cover  the  following: 

Part    1   Determination  of  pyrometric  cone  equivalent  (  PCE  )  or  softening  point 
Part    2  Determination  of  refractoriness  under  load 
Part    3  Determination  of  spalling  resistance 
Part    4  Determination  of  cold  crushing  strength 
Part    5  Determination  of  modulus  of  rupture 
Part    6  Determination  of  permanent  change  after  reheating 
Part    7   Methods  of  sampling  and  criteria  for  conformity 
Part    8  Determination  of  apparent  porosity 
Part    9  Determination  of  true  specific  gravity  and  true  density 
Part  10  Determination  of  size  of  refractory  bricks 
Part  12  Determination  of  bulk^density 

Part  13  Determination  of  resistance  to  the  disintegrating  effect  of  carbon  monoxide 
Part  14   Determination  of  sieve  analysis 

Part  16  Determination  of  thermal  conductivity  upto  1  250®C  of  dense  and  insulating  refractory 
products  according  to  the  hot  wire  parallel  method 

Part  19  Determination  of  thermal  expansion 

In  this  revision  the  apparatus  and  procedure  has  been  modified,  which  is  more  precise. 

In  reporting  the  result  ofatestor  analysis  made  in  accordance  with  this  standjard,  the  final  value, 
observed  or  calculated,  is  to  be  rounded  off  in  accordance  with  IS  2  :  I960  'Rules  for  rounding  off 
numerical  values  {  revised  )\ 


IS  1528  (  Part  11  )  :  1993 


Indian  Standard 


METHODS  OF  SAMPLING  AND  PHYSICAL 
TESTS  FOR  REFRACTORY  MATERIALS 

PART  11     DETERMINATION  OF  WARPAGE 

f  Second  Revision  ) 


1  SCOPE 

This  standard  (Part  11  )  prescribes  the  method 
of  test  for  determination  of  warpage. 

2  REFERENCES 

The  following  Indian  Standards  are  necessary 
adjuncts  to  this  standard:

3  TERMINOLOGY 

For  the  purpose  of  this  standard,  the  definitions 
given  in  IS  4041  :  1987  shall  apply. 

4  DETERMINATION  OF  WARPAGE 

4.1  Apparatus 

The  apparatus  consists  of  a  wooden  platform, 
top  covered  by  thick  glass  plate  having  dimen- 
sion 500  X  250  mm.  Any  other  dimension  can 
also  be  considered  for  big  size  sample  accom- 
modation. At  the  side  of  the  plate  the  metallic 
rod  fixed  perpendicularly  to  the  plate  holds  dial 
gauge  which  can  be  adjusted  up  and  down  along 
the  rod  and  fixed  at  the  desired  height.  The  dial 
gauge  can  measure  minimum  length  0-01  mm 
and  maximum  length  13-5  mm. 

4.2  Procedure 

The  sample  with  concave  side  up  is  placed  on 
the  glass  plate  (  see  Fig.  i  ).  Any  two  points  at 
the  diagonals  or  at  any  straight  line  parallel  to 
length  or  breadth  with  their  mid  points  are 
marked  on  the  concave  surface.  The  dial  gauge 
is  adjusted  in  such  a  way  that  reading  can  be 
taken  at  the  above  three  points.  During 
measurement  the  position  of  the  dial  gauge 
should  be  fixed  and  sample  should  be  moved 
slowly  over  the  glass  plate  (  see  Fig.  2  )  so  that 
three  readings  at  A,  B,  and  C  points  can  be 
taken.

Calculate  the  warpage  for  each  of  the  diagonal 
positions  or  of  any  chosen  positions  as  follows:

Standard  Mark 

The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  provisions  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian 
Standards  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  thereunder.  The  Standard  Mark  on 
products  covered  by  an  Indian  Standard  conveys  the  assurance  that  they  have  been 
produced  to  comply  with  the  requirements  of  that  standard  under  a  well  defined  system  of 
inspection,  testing  and  quality  control  which  is  devised  and  supervised  by  BIS  and  operated 
by  the  producer.  Standard  marked  products  are  also  continuously  checked  by  BIS  for  con- 
formity to  that  standard  as  a  further  safeguard.  Details  of  conditions  under  which  a  licence 
for  the  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  producers  may  be 
obtained  from  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 


Bareaii  of  ladiaa  Standards 

BIS  is  a  statutory  institutioti  established  uader  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  AcU  i9S6  to  promote 
harmonious  development  of  the  activities  of  standardization,  marking  and  quality  certification  of 
goods  and  attending  to  connected  matters  in  the  country. 

Copyright 

BIS  has  the  copyright  of  all  its  publications.  No  part  of  these  publications  may  be  reproduced  in  any 
form  without  the  prior  permission  in  writing  of  BIS.  This  does  not  preclude  the  free  use,  in  the  course  of 
implementing  the  standard,  of  necessary  details,  such  as  symbols  and  sizes,  type  or  grade  designations. 
Enquiries  relating  to  copyright  be  addressed  to  the  Director  (  Publications  ),  BIS. 

Review  of  Indian  Standards 

Amendments  are  issued  to  standards  as  the  need  arises  on  the  basis  of  comments.  Standards  are  also 
reviewed  periodically;  a  standard  along  with  amendments  is  reaffirmed  when  such  review  indicates  thai 
no  changes  are  needed;  if  the  review  indicates  that  changes  are  needed,  it  is  taken  up  for  revision. 
Users  of  Indian  Standards  should  ascertain  that  they  are  in  possession  of  the  latest  amendments  or 
edition  by  referring  to  the  latest  issue  of  *BIS  Handbook*  and  ^Standards  Monthly  Additions* 
Comments  on  this  Indian  Standard  may  be  sent  to  BIS  giving  the  following  reference]
